 Shopee & Hyundai Glovis Partner to Boost K-Beauty Exports in Asia
 By: Asia Business Outlook Team | Monday, 26 October 2026 
 South Korean logistics company Hyundai Glovis has partnered with Shopee Korea to help local cosmetics brands sell their products in Southeast Asia.
 The partnership aims to make exporting easier by bringing transportation, customs clearance and delivery services under one system. The service began operations in October 2026.
 The move comes as K-beauty products continue to attract customers across international markets. Shopee gives Korean brands access to consumers across Southeast Asia and other regions, while Hyundai Glovis provides the logistics support needed to deliver products overseas.
 Together, the companies aim to help businesses reach more customers and manage international orders more easily.
 Key Highlights 
 Shopee and Hyundai Glovis Partner to Expand K-Beauty Exports 
 Hyundai Glovis, Shopee Simplify Korean Cosmetics Exports 
 Shopee Partnership Helps Korean Beauty Brands Reach Global Markets 
 One-Stop Logistics Service for Korean Brands 
 Under the partnership, Hyundai Glovis will handle several stages of the export process, from collecting products in South Korea to shipping them overseas and arranging delivery. Its logistics services include domestic transportation, air and sea freight, customs clearance, local regulatory procedures, warehousing and order fulfilment.
 Previously, cosmetics companies often had to work with several service providers to manage these tasks. Coordinating different companies could increase costs, create delays and make the export process more complicated, particularly for smaller businesses.
 The new service brings these activities together, allowing sellers to manage their shipping requirements through a single logistics partner. Hyundai Glovis expects the arrangement to reduce delivery times and ease the workload for businesses looking to sell overseas.
 Meeting local regulations is another challenge for Korean cosmetics brands. Each market has its own import rules and product requirements, which companies must understand before entering a new country. By helping sellers manage these procedures alongside shipping and delivery, Hyundai Glovis aims to make international expansion less complicated.
 The arrangement will also allow businesses to spend more time on product development, marketing and sales rather than managing multiple logistics providers. For smaller brands, this could make it easier to explore new markets and build a customer base outside South Korea.
 Partnership Plans to Reach More Markets 
 Shopee and Hyundai Glovis plan to expand the service beyond Southeast Asia into other regions, including Central and South America. This could give Korean cosmetics brands more opportunities to sell internationally while relying on a single partner for much of their logistics needs.
 The agreement also supports Hyundai Glovis' efforts to grow its business beyond companies affiliated with Hyundai Motor Group, including Hyundai Motor and Kia. By working with more external customers, the company hopes to diversify its revenue sources and strengthen its position in the global logistics market .
 Hyundai Glovis aims to increase the share of revenue it earns from non-affiliated customers to 40% of total sales by 2030. To achieve this, the company is looking to use its transportation network and supply chain services to attract businesses from different industries.
 Its work with consumer goods and entertainment products is part of this strategy. The company has expanded its logistics services to include cosmetics and K-pop albums shipped to overseas markets. The Shopee partnership builds on these efforts by connecting its logistics network with an established e-commerce platform.
 Logistics Plays a Key Role in K-Beauty Growth 
 For Shopee, the partnership gives Korean sellers another option for managing international deliveries. For Hyundai Glovis, it creates an opportunity to work with more businesses that need cross-border shipping and fulfilment services.
 The agreement also reflects the growing importance of e-commerce logistics in online retail. As more companies sell products directly to customers in other countries, reliable shipping, efficient customs clearance and timely delivery have become important parts of the shopping experience.
 Korean beauty products have gained attention in international markets, creating opportunities for brands of different sizes. However, reaching overseas customers involves more than offering popular products. Companies must also deal with shipping costs, import regulations and delivery expectations in each market.

 By combining Shopee's online marketplace with Hyundai Glovis' logistics services, the companies aim to make this process easier for Korean cosmetics sellers. Their planned expansion into additional regions could open up more opportunities for K-beauty exports and support the growth of Southeast Asian e-commerce .
